text: Avant la décision 2021-0116 sur les fréquences utilisateurs, l'Arcep avait autorisé des stations terriennes passerelles Starlink en France, d'abord au nom de TIBRO France SARL. Pour chaque station (Belin-Béliet, Gravelines, Villenave-d'Ornon, Saint-Senier-de-Beuvron), donnez le numéro et la date de la décision d'attribution, les bandes et la durée, la décision qui a remplacé TIBRO par Starlink France SARL, et, le cas échéant, le numéro et la date de la décision d'abrogation. Combien de ces quatre autorisations restent en vigueur au 9 octobre 2026 ? Ne vous fiez pas aux articles de presse qui parlent de « trois stations prévues » : comptez les décisions.
reference: Nine Arcep decisions, all on arcep.fr/uploads/tx_gsavis/. Attributions: Belin-Béliet 2020-0727 du 30 juin 2020; Gravelines 2020-0744 du 2 juillet 2020; Villenave-d'Ornon 2020-0884 du 17 août 2020; Saint-Senier-de-Beuvron 2020-1452 du 1er décembre 2020 (this one already in the name of Starlink France SARL). All four: bandes 18 GHz et 28 GHz, durée de dix ans à compter de la décision, satellite STEAM-2B, renewal request at least four months before expiry. Annex replacements: 2020-0764 and 2020-0765 du 8 juillet 2020 (Belin-Béliet, Gravelines), no change of duration. Name change: 2020-1415 du 26 novembre 2020 replaces TIBRO France SARL by Starlink France SARL in 2020-0727, 2020-0744 and 2020-0884 without changing durations (note: its recitals wrongly place Gravelines in Gironde; the attribution says Nord 59). Abrogations: Belin-Béliet by 2021-0062 du 14 janvier 2021; Saint-Senier by 2022-0032 du 4 janvier 2022; Gravelines by 2022-0182 du 20 janvier 2022, all at Starlink's request. Villenave-d'Ornon (2020-0884) is the only one not abrogated in these records, so one of four remains, expiring 17 August 2030 absent renewal. Wrong: three stations only (Belin-Béliet is the fourth, abrogated a year before the others); wrong: abrogations dated to the Conseil d'État ruling of April 2022 (that annulled 2021-0116, not these); wrong: TIBRO as the holder of 2020-1452. Sources: https://www.arcep.fr/uploads/tx_gsavis/20-0727.pdf, 20-0744.pdf, 20-0884.pdf, 20-0764.pdf, 20-0765.pdf, 20-1415.pdf, 20-1452.pdf, 21-0062.pdf, 22-0032.pdf, 22-0182.pdf (same path).

text: Starlink Chile SpA ha pedido a la Subtel modificar dos concesiones distintas para instalar estaciones terrenas (gateways) Ka y banda E. Para cada uno de los extractos 24-SP157939, 25-SP69683 y 25-SP69681 indique: qué decreto supremo (número y año) y qué tipo de concesión se modifica, cuántos gateways se piden y en qué comunas, la fecha y número del Diario Oficial cuando el extracto lo trae, y el número de domos (antenas) declarado por estación. Diga también qué restricción geográfica aplica a los gateways en 71-76 / 81-86 GHz según la nota 5 citada. Ojo: el nombre de una estación no coincide con su comuna.
reference: Three Subtel/Diario Oficial extracts. 24-SP157939 (PDF on subtel.gob.cl, signed 17 Jan 2025; no Diario Oficial masthead in the file): modifies the concesión de Servicio Público de Transmisión de Datos granted by decreto supremo N° 156 de 2021; four gateways: Space X San Bernardo 1 (San Bernardo), Limache 1 (Limache), Cabrero 1 (comuna Chillán Viejo, Región de Ñuble, not Cabrero), Pudahuel 1 (Pudahuel); each station between 8 and 40 Gateway V4 domes. 25-SP69683: Diario Oficial Núm. 44.235, miércoles 27 de agosto de 2025, CVE 2690368; modifies the concesión de Servicio Intermedio de Telecomunicaciones granted by decreto supremo N° 5 de 2025; six gateways with antenna counts: San Bernardo 1 (30), Limache 1 (10), Cabrero 1 (20), Pudahuel 1 (20), Las Condes 1 (20), Quilicura 1 (30). 25-SP69681: Diario Oficial Núm. 44.406, sábado 21 de marzo de 2026, CVE 2785277; modifies DS 156/2021 again; one gateway, SpaceX Las Condes 1 (Las Condes, Parque Natural La Plaza Sur), 20 domes. All three: Ka uplink 27,5-29,1 and 29,5-30 GHz, downlink 17,8-18,6 and 18,8-19,3 GHz; E band 81-86 up / 71-76 down; plazos 1 mes obras, 22 meses término, 24 meses servicio from publication of the authorising decree. Nota 5 of Res. Ex. 6.966/2009 art. 2: in 71-76 and 81-86 GHz only gateways located from the Región de Coquimbo southwards, with possible minimum-elevation limits to protect ALMA. Wrong: treating the three as one concession; putting Cabrero 1 in the comuna of Cabrero; claiming any of these extracts is the granting decree (they are requests open to 30 días hábiles of opposition). Sources: https://www.subtel.gob.cl/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/SSPP-Extracto-de-solicitud-24-SP157939-de-modificacion-de-concesion-de-Servicio-Publico-de-Transmision-de-Datos-a-STARLINK-CHILE-SpA-que-incorpora-estaciones-terrenas-en-distintas-comunas.pdf ; https://www.subtel.gob.cl/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/2690368.pdf ; https://www.subtel.gob.cl/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Solicitud-numero-25-SP69681.-Starlink-Chile-SpA.pdf

text: Starlink is licensed in several small British-linked jurisdictions through different corporate entities and licence types. For Guernsey (GCRA), Jersey (JCRA), the Cayman Islands (URCO/OfReg), the Turks and Caicos Islands (Telecommunications Commission) and the Falkland Islands, give the licensee's exact legal name, the licence type or class, the date the licence was decided or took effect, and one distinctive condition or term from the document (for example term length, spectrum listed, or MNO partnership). For Cayman, also state what Amendment No. 1 added and its date. Do not assume the same Irish company holds all of them.
reference: Five jurisdictions, six documents. Guernsey: GCRA case T1582G, notice of proposed decision dated 8 June 2022 to grant Starlink Internet Services Limited (registered in Ireland, Dublin address) a fixed telecommunications licence for satellite user-terminal network and ESIM services; comments by 15 June 2022; became final from 22 June 2022; Ku band under its Ofcom Earth Station Network licence which covers the Channel Islands. Jersey: JCRA case T-050, Final Notice JCRA 24/23 issued 3 April 2024 (order dated 27 March 2024), Class II licence under the Telecommunications (Jersey) Law 2002 to Starlink Internet Services Limited (Irish company 677409); licence commencement 3 May 2024; term 15 years from commencement; Sure (Jersey) objected on 15 February 2024 to the omission of the local-management condition. Cayman: licence to Starlink (Cayman Islands) Limited dated 22 December 2025 (press release 23 December 2025 says Starlink Cayman Islands Ltd), first under the satellite service provider framework; Amendment No. 1 dated 28 May 2026 adds non-exclusive MSS frequencies for direct-to-device (1518-1559, 1626.5-1660.5, 1668-1675, 1990-2010, 2180-2200, 2483.5-2500 MHz) alongside Ku 10700-12700 / 14000-14500 MHz in Annex 4. Turks and Caicos: Decision Notice 2026-8 of 19 August 2026, Starlink Caribbean LLC, Satellite Network/Service Licence and Spectrum Licence (shared basis), 10.7-12.7 GHz (2000 MHz) and 14.0-14.5 GHz (500 MHz); Board approved 12 August 2026, Minister 14 August 2026; D2D requires partnership with at least one local MNO; framework DN 2026-2 of 20 March 2026, resubmission 23 March 2026. Falklands: FIG statement 30 October 2025, VSAT Broadband Connectivity Licence to Starlink Internet Services Limited; Regulator resumed issuing VSAT licences 3 November 2025 from midday; Sure may claim up to £6.167m. Wrong: one entity everywhere (Cayman and TCI use local entities); wrong: Jersey Class III; wrong: TCI licence dated March 2026. Sources: https://www.gcra.gg/media/598605/starlink-telco-licence-application-notice-of-proposed-decision.pdf ; https://www.jcra.je/media/598928/t-050-final-notice-issuing-a-class-ii-licence-to-starlink-internet-services-limited.pdf ; https://www.jcra.je/media/598929/t-050-starlink-internet-services-limited-class-ii-licence.pdf ; https://www.ofreg.ky/viewPDF/documents/2025-12-23-17-23-27-PressReleaseSateliteStarlink-FINAL.pdf ; https://www.ofreg.ky/viewPDF/documents/2026-08-05-20-58-25-AMENDMENT-No-1-TO-THE-LICENCE-OF--STARLINK.pdf ; https://telecommission.tc/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-19-V2-Final-Decision-Notice-2026-8-Starlink-SNS-Application-.pdf ; FIG statement reproduced at https://openfalklands.com/fig-press-statement-fig-and-sure-reach-vsat-licensing-agreement/ (original PDF on falklands.gov.fk was unreachable on 9 Oct 2026).

text: ComReg handled Starlink's second Irish gateway in 2025. Using ComReg's own documents, give: the date ComReg received the Killala application and the information notice number and date; the Killala site coordinates and antenna diameter; the consultation closing date and time; the four centre frequencies already licensed at Garrettstown with bandwidth and EIRP; the number and date of the notice containing ComReg's final view, who the only respondent was, and what ComReg said it would do. Do not report the 27 May 2025 notice as a grant.
reference: Three ComReg documents. ComReg 25/31, Information Notice dated 27/05/2025: application received 19 March 2025 from Starlink Internet Services Limited for an SES licence in the 18 GHz (17.7-19.7 space-to-Earth) and 28 GHz (27.5-29.5 Earth-to-space) bands at Killala, Co. Mayo; Table 2 gives Lat/Long 54.194077, -9.2114458, site height 49.75 m AMSL, antenna diameter 1.85 m, elevation 20-90 degrees; consultation runs until 17:00 on 25 June 2025; ComReg's preliminary view was that it would not cause harmful interference and it proposed to grant. Table 1, Garrettstown, Co Cork licensed frequencies: 27.75, 28.3, 28.85 and 29.75 GHz, each 500 MHz bandwidth, each 67 dBW EIRP. A fixed link at the same Killala site operates 17727.5/18737.5 MHz (28 MHz). ComReg 25/36R (20 June 2025) is the parallel Amazon Kuiper notice. ComReg 25/79, Information Notice dated 04/11/2025: ViaSat Inc. was the only interested party to respond to either notice (Article 22 EPFD arguments); ComReg's final view is that it will grant SES licences to Amazon and Starlink and publish on its Siteviewer portal; it notes Inmarsat/Space Norway (Viasat group) told Ofcom they had coordination agreements with Starlink. Wrong: a licence number or grant date in 25/31; a respondent other than Viasat; EPFD assessment performed by ComReg (it says that sits with the ITU and DCCS). Sources: https://www.comreg.ie/media/2025/05/ComReg-25_31.pdf (also at https://www.comreg.ie/publication-download/starlink-internet-services-limited-application-for-a-satellite-earth-station-licence) ; https://www.comreg.ie/publication-download/satellite-earth-station-licences-amazon-kuiper-services-europe-sarl-and-starlink-internet-services-limited (ComReg 25/79).

text: CRAN refused Starlink's Namibian licence in March 2026 and then closed a reconsideration round in June. From the Government Gazette notice and CRAN's own releases, give: the gazette number, notice number and date; the two licences declined and the frequency ranges and Namibian ownership percentage shown; the date the applications were lodged and which of the six criteria were met and not met; how many public reconsideration requests were received and how many were dismissed on procedural grounds; the date Starlink filed its own request, why it was dismissed, and the deadline date CRAN gave. Note where CRAN's own documents disagree on the reconsideration window, and do not rely on news reports for whether Starlink itself filed.
reference: Four primary documents. Government Gazette No. 8872, 23 March 2026, General Notice No. 197: CRAN declined a Class Comprehensive Telecommunications Service Licence (ECS and ECNS) and a Spectrum Licence for Starlink Internet Services Namibia (Pty) Limited; table shows United States of America incorporation, 0% Namibian ownership, 10.7-14.7 GHz applied, downlink 10.7-12.7 GHz (2000 MHz), uplink 14.0-14.5 GHz (500 MHz), national, fixed-satellite; reconsideration under section 31 'within 90 days of this notice'. Media release 24 March 2026: applications submitted 1 June 2024; met competition, technical and financial capacity, frequency availability; not met ownership and control (section 46, 51% Namibian, no exemption), national defence and public security, compliance history (operating without a licence, ignoring a summons); 3 of 6 criteria; reconsideration 'within thirty (30) days, from 23 March 2026'. Media release 8 June 2026 (page dated 11 June): 624 public applications received and Starlink's own application received 'today', i.e. 8 June 2026. Media release 22 June 2026: 622 of 624 dismissed for failing procedural and jurisdictional requirements, two assessed on merits with no new facts; Starlink's own application dismissed as lodged outside the statutory period with no power to condone; a petition of 17 June 2026 also late; release says the deadline 'expired on 23 April 2026' while the CEO remarks of the same day say the 30 days lapsed on 22 April 2026; section 46(2) exemptions are for the Minister; remedy is High Court review under section 32. Internal inconsistency to flag: 90 days (gazette) vs 30 days (releases), and 22 vs 23 April. Wrong: that Starlink never filed (some press repeated an earlier CRAN line); that the appeal was decided on the merits. Sources: https://www.cran.na/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/8872-Gen-N196-198-23-Mar-2026.pdf ; https://www.cran.na/download/cran-concludes-assessment-of-starlink-licence-application-24-march-2026-windhoek/ ; https://www.cran.na/download/updated-cran-receives-reconsideration-applications-including-from-starlink-regarding-licence-decision/ ; https://www.cran.na/download/media-release-cran-confirms-dismissal-of-starlink-reconsideration-requests-22-jun-2026/ ; https://www.cran.na/download/ceo-remarks-starlink-decision-22-jun-2026/

text: En México, Starlink Satellite Systems México, S. de R.L. de C.V. opera bajo tres títulos distintos del IFT inscritos en el Registro Público de Concesiones. Para la autorización IFT/223/UCS/AUT-SAT-EXT-029/2021, su modificación IFT/223/UCS/1262/2022 y la concesión única P/IFT/070721/319, indique: fecha de otorgamiento, vigencia (10 o 30 años), redes satelitales (expedientes UIT) y bandas de frecuencia que cada uno ampara, la reserva del Estado fijada, y la fecha y número de inscripción de la modificación en el Registro. ¿La modificación de 2022 amplió la banda Ku/Ka de Starlink o añadió otra cosa? No confunda la constelación añadida con los satélites de banda ancha de Starlink.
reference: Three IFT instruments on the Registro Público (rpc.ift.org.mx now redirects to rpc.crt.gob.mx). Autorización IFT/223/UCS/AUT-SAT-EXT-029/2021: application 2 April 2021; oficio IFT/223/UCS/952/2021 of 24 May 2021; the 2022 resolution records it as granted 28 May 2021; vigencia diez años, extendable for equal terms; condición 1.8 no exclusivity; Reserva del Estado condición 5.1: 5% of ingresos brutos tarifados paid semi-annually; Anexo Técnico lists Constelación SpaceX-Starlink, redes STEAM-1, STEAM-2 and STEAM-2B, downlink 10700-12700 MHz (Ku) and 17800-18600 / 18800-19300 MHz (Ka), uplink 14000-14500 MHz (Ku) and 27500-29100 / 29500-30000 MHz (Ka), Fijo por Satélite, national coverage. Modificación IFT/223/UCS/1262/2022 dated 4 de julio de 2022: request filed 19 May 2022; resolves to authorise modification to include the ITU network USASAT-NGSO-7 operated through the SWARM constellation (SWARM-1), downlink 137-138 MHz, uplink 148-150 MHz, Móvil por Satélite, 30 kHz capacity, PIRE 1.76 dBW; the Secretaría said the Reserva del Estado of 5% need not change; registered in the Registro Público de Concesiones on 10 de agosto de 2022, inscripción 061647, folio FET100298AU-519564. So the 2022 act added a narrowband MSS IoT network, not more Ku/Ka spectrum. Concesión única P/IFT/070721/319: approved unanimously at the XIII Sesión Ordinaria del Pleno on 07 de julio de 2021; application filed 19 December 2020 for a network using Ka and Ku satellite capacity with national coverage; Resolutivo Primero grants a título de concesión única para uso comercial for 30 (treinta) años to provide any telecommunications or broadcasting service with national coverage; it does not itself confer spectrum de uso determinado or orbital resources, which must be obtained separately under the Ley Federal de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión; the resolution notes the May 2021 authorization already covered Ka and Ku. Wrong: saying the 2022 modification covers Gen2 or E-band; saying USASAT-NGSO-3X appears in either document (it does not); giving the registry date as the resolution date. Sources: https://rpc.crt.gob.mx/vrpc/pdfs/100298_210621144132_9550.pdf ; https://rpc.crt.gob.mx/vrpc/pdfs/100298_220812175852_1878.pdf ; https://www.ift.org.mx/sites/default/files/conocenos/pleno/sesiones/acuerdoliga/pift070721319.pdf

text: Between 2022 and 2024 Ofcom granted, then saw surrendered, then varied Starlink's UK Ka-band gateway licences. From Ofcom's November 2022 statement, its April 2024 consultation and its 1 August 2024 statement, list: the six sites granted in 2022 and how many UK gateways SpaceX had before and after; the two sites surrendered and when; the four licences varied in 2024 with their licence numbers, the antenna count before and after at each, and the Ka-band ranges stated in 2024; which company name holds the Isle of Man licence; and who responded to the 2024 consultation. Do not merge these with the 2025 E-band or 2026 Harlow decisions.
reference: Three Ofcom documents. Statement 10 November 2022 'Decision on applications for six non-geostationary earth station gateway licences': applications received 27 May 2022 from Starlink Internet Services Limited; six sites Bristol, Fawley, Hoo St Werburgh, Morn Hill, Wherstead, Woodwalton; SpaceX already operated three UK gateways (licences held by Arqiva at Chalfont, Goonhilly, and Starlink) so the grant takes it to nine; Ka ranges applied 27.5-27.8185, 28.4545-28.8265 and 29.4625-30 GHz; licences issued on payment of fee; gateways must commence within 12 months. Consultation 26 April 2024 (closing 31 May 2024): Starlink surrendered Bristol and Hoo St Werburgh in October 2023; variation sought for Fawley (licence 1293217), Isle of Man (249304/1), Wherstead (1293534), Woodwalton (1293303); each currently up to 9 Ka-band antennas; Fawley, Wherstead, Woodwalton to add 24 for 32 each; Isle of Man to add 32 for 40; bands 27.5-28.0525, 28.4445-29.0605, 29.4525-30 GHz (wider than 2022 because gateway spectrum was added to the licences in March 2023); Table 3 lists seven remaining gateways, with the Isle of Man held by Starlink Internet Services UK Limited and the others by Starlink Internet Services Limited; Chalfont (Arqiva) and Goonhilly are not Starlink licences. Statement 1 August 2024: approves the variation for all four sites; Viasat was the respondent published. Wrong: nine sites still licensed; Morn Hill among the varied sites; the 2022 band edges quoted as the 2024 ones; Isle of Man licence in the Irish company's name. Sources: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/__data/assets/pdf_file/0029/247178/statement-starlink-ngso-application.pdf ; https://www.ofcom.org.uk/__data/assets/pdf_file/0031/283729/consultation-spacex-application-ngso-gateway-licence-april24.pdf ; https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/consultations/category-3-4-weeks/283714-starlink-internet-services-limited-spacex-application/associated-documents/statement-starlink-internet-services-limited-spacex.pdf ; page https://www.ofcom.org.uk/spectrum/space-and-satellites/spacex-application-variation-non-geostationary-gateway-licence

text: Starlink Argentina S.R.L. no obtuvo su licencia TIC por un acto directo sino por transferencia, y en 2026 recibió dos actos más del ENACOM. Para las Resoluciones ENACOM 4/2024, 372/2026 y 663/2026 indique: fecha de firma, fecha de publicación en el Boletín Oficial, expediente, qué dispone cada una (qué resoluciones previas se citan en la transferencia; qué autoriza la 372 y con qué carácter; qué proyecto aprueba la 663, el monto total y cómo se reparte entre donación y FSU), y el firmante. No confunda la 663/2026 con la resolución posterior que aprobó el convenio.
reference: Three ENACOM resolutions. Resolución Sintetizada 4/2024, RESOL-2024-4-APN-ENACOM#JGM, fecha 23/2/2024, Boletín Oficial 26/02/2024 (e. 26/02/2024 N° 8799/24): 1) inscribe TIBRO NETHERLANDS B.V. SUCURSAL ARGENTINA in the Registro de Servicios TIC for Servicio Fijo y Móvil por Satélite; 2) authorises Tibro to transfer the licence and registrations of Servicio Fijo Satelital, Valor Agregado - Acceso a Internet, and Fijo y Móvil por Satélite, granted by Resoluciones N° 1291/2020 and 1157/2023, to STARLINK ARGENTINA S.R.L.; signed Juan Martín Ozores, Interventor. Resolución Sintetizada 372/2026, RESOL-2026-372-APN-ENACOM#JGM, fecha 28/05/2026, expediente EX-2025-139631951-APN-DGDYD#JGM, Boletín Oficial 01/06/2026 (N° 36841/26): authorises Starlink Argentina S.R.L. 'con carácter de excepción' to operate in requested frequency segments not yet attributed to the Servicio Fijo por Satélite in Argentina, subject to conditions in article 2 (no harmful interference and no protection, RNI limits, protect radio astronomy per footnote 5.149, tied to the sites and parameters of the application; any change needs a new electromagnetic compatibility analysis), under apercibimiento de caducidad; signed Ozores. The published extract names no band; law-firm notes call it W band. Resolución 663/2026, RESOL-2026-663-APN-ENACOM#JGM, signed 24 de julio de 2026 (digital signature Ozores 2026.07.24), EX-2026-71541314-APN-DNPYD#ENACOM, Boletín Oficial 29/07/2026 in extract: approves the Proyecto Específico 'CONECTIVIDAD SATELITAL EN ESTABLECIMIENTOS EDUCATIVOS DE GESTIÓN PÚBLICA DE LA REPÚBLICA ARGENTINA' under programme C.I.P. (Res. 1072/24); assigns USD 21.876.000 from the FSU: USD 9.978.000 as a donación con cargo by Starlink Argentina S.R.L. (CUIT 30-71754087-1) for 6.000 kits, accessories and 24 months of service, and USD 11.898.000 of FSU funds for installation, service management, technical support, an API platform and 12 further months of service. The convenio and donation contract were approved later by Resolución 857/2026 (2 September 2026), not by 663. Wrong: a direct licence to Starlink in 2024; a general W-band attribution; reading USD 9.978.000 as 'millones'. Sources: https://www.boletinoficial.gob.ar/detalleAviso/primera/304028/20240226 ; https://www.boletinoficial.gob.ar/detalleAviso/primera/342644/20260601 ; https://www.boletinoficial.gob.ar/detalleAviso/primera/345097/20260729 ; full text of 663/2026 at https://www.cabase.org.ar/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Resolucion-ENACOM-663-2026.pdf

text: A Starlink tem três frentes abertas na Anatel sobre o Direito de Exploração de Satélite Estrangeiro do sistema Starlink: o pedido Gen2 relatado pelo conselheiro Alexandre Freire (processo 53500.114602/2023-73), a Consulta Pública nº 9/2026 e a Consulta Pública nº 29/2026. Para cada uma indique: número(s) de processo, data do pedido ou do ato, data de publicação no DOU (seção, edição e página quando houver), o que exatamente se pede (número de satélites, faixas de subida e descida ou bloco em MHz), prazo de contribuição e quem assina. Diferencie claramente as faixas da CP 9 das faixas Ku/Ka/E já autorizadas, e não trate as consultas como autorizações concedidas.
reference: Three documents. Relatório SEI nº 12964217 (signed 02/12/2024 by Alexandre Reis Siqueira Freire), Processo nº 53500.114602/2023-73, interessado Starlink Brazil Holding Ltda.: request of 26 December 2023 (SEI 11313487) for 7.500 new non-geostationary satellites (Gen2) and addition of 71-76 GHz (descida) and 81-86 GHz (subida), Banda E; Anatel opened Consulta Pública nº 38 de 19 de julho de 2024 (processo 53500.057247/2024-17) under Ato nº 4.430/2023; sent to the Conselho Diretor 12 November 2024 (Matéria para Apreciação nº 928/2024) and distributed 14 November 2024. (The Conselho approved on 8 April 2025, Acórdão 91, with a public price of R$ 102.677 and validity to 28 March 2027 per press and the earlier audit prompt; the relatório itself predates that.) Consulta Pública nº 9, de 23 de fevereiro de 2026, DOU 27/02/2026, Seção 1, edição 39, página 14, signed by Vinicius Oliveira Caram Guimarães, Superintendente de Outorga e Recursos à Prestação; processos 53500.003778/2026-43 and 53500.011767/2026-37; requester Starlink Brazil Holding LTDA. for Space Exploration Holdings LLC; new uplink 12,70-13,25; 13,75-14; 14,50-14,80; 15,43-15,63; 29,10-29,50; 47,20-50,20; 50,40-51,40 GHz and downlink 17,70-17,80; 18,60-18,80; 19,30-20,20; 37,50-39,50; 40-42,50 GHz; 'mais de mil satélites'; 10 days from publication (press: until 9 March 2026). Consulta Pública nº 29, de 8 de julho de 2026, DOU 10/07/2026, Seção 1, edição 128, página 63, signed by Sidney Azeredo Nince (substituto); processos 53500.062879/2026-56 and 53500.020054/2026-64; Banda S for direct-to-device, a 10 + 10 MHz block in the lower portion of the S band, with a question on whether 15 + 15 MHz in 1.980-1.995 / 2.170-2.185 MHz is needed; 10 days. Wrong: presenting CP 9 or CP 29 as granted; listing E band among CP 9 bands; dating CP 9 by the signature date as the publication date. Sources: https://static.poder360.com.br/2025/04/relatorio-anatel-starlink.pdf (copy of SEI 12964217, verifiable at anatel.gov.br/autenticidade with CRC 7D75EF58) ; DOU texts mirrored at https://atlaspublico.com.br/regulacao/dou/consulta-publica-n-9-de-23-de-fevereiro-de-2026-291132 and https://atlaspublico.com.br/regulacao/dou/consulta-publica-n-29-de-8-de-julho-de-2026-621308 (official: in.gov.br DOU of 27/02/2026 and 10/07/2026).

text: SpaceX Services runs two dual-band gateways on rolling special temporary authority: Hillsboro, Oregon (call sign E250202) and Atlanta, Georgia (call sign E250226). From the Space Bureau's weekly Actions Taken notices, list every STA the Bureau granted for those two call signs during 2026 up to 9 October 2026: file number, date filed, date of action, and the authorized term if the notice gives one. Flag any grant that has no term because it was made under section 1.62 to cover continuing operations. text: La Commission européenne a adopté le 27 mai 2026 une proposition de règlement sur l'autorisation des systèmes mobiles par satellite dans la bande 2 GHz. La définition d'« incumbent » à l'article 2 couvre-t-elle une entreprise qui a légalement acquis le contrôle d'un titulaire, ce qui importe pour SpaceX et EchoStar ? Enfin, combien de blocs appariés de 5 MHz l'article 4 met en jeu, combien sont réservés en priorité au système MSS/hybride sécurisé, et quelle durée l'article 16 fixe aux nouveaux droits ? Ne présentez pas ce texte comme un règlement adopté : c'est une proposition.
reference: Hop 1: Commission press/library page (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/proposal-eu-level-authorisation-systems-providing-mobile-satellite-services-mss) leads to the text; Council register copy ST 9777 2026 INIT (https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-9777-2026-INIT/en/pdf). Hop 2 (inside the text): recital (3) says that under Decision No 626/2008/EC two undertakings were selected in 2009 by Commission Decision 2009/449/EC (footnote: Commission Decision of 13 May 2009) and authorised to use each a paired block of 15 MHz 'in all Member States until May 2027'. Article 20(1) (Transitory provisions): 'The duration of the existing rights of use granted in accordance with Decision 2009/449/EC to the incumbents, Viasat and Echostar, are extended, upon request, for a period of two years, under the authorisation conditions applicable at the date of entry into force of this Regulation'; 'during this extension period the rights shall not be transferred, nor leased or sub-leased'; Commission Decision 2011/667 continues to apply; Art 20(2) lets the Commission impose sharing conditions for testing/experimental use. text: Under the 6 October 2026 D2D authorization, SpaceX will provide supplemental coverage from space on its own unpaired AWS-3 (1695-1710 MHz) and AWS-H Block licenses without any terrestrial partner. Press coverage says the FCC 'waived the spectrum leasing rule'; the conditions are more specific than that.
reference:
Grade DA-26-1078 (6 October 2026), grant conditions 1(b), 1(c), 1(d), 1(e) and Order paragraphs 12-37.

Rules waived: condition 1(b) waives 47 CFR 25.125(a) and (b) (lease arrangement with a terrestrial licensee) for SCS in the AWS-3 and AWS-H bands, because SpaceX will hold both the satellite and terrestrial licenses (paragraph 14). Condition 1(c) waives 2.106(a) and (d)(33)(i) (the unpaired AWS-3 band is not allocated for SCS), 27.77 (mobiles in 1695-1710 MHz may operate only under control of an enabling base station) and 25.125(a)/(b) (the GIA requirement that the terrestrial licensee hold all co-channel licenses throughout CONUS). Condition 1(e) waives section 25.115 so handsets need no separate earth station authorization and, on the Bureaus' own motion, 25.115(q) for AWS-3 SCS earth stations.

Federal protection: condition 1(c)(i) - SpaceX is not authorized to provide SCS or transmit any signal that enables mobiles to transmit in 1695-1710 MHz in a Federal Protection Zone listed in section 27.1134 unless and until it reaches a written coordination agreement with the relevant Federal incumbents; it must accept interference and immediately terminate on notification of harmful interference. Paragraph 18: 47 Federal earth stations and 27 Protection Zones; paragraph 26 says the coordination trigger is SpaceX proposing to have a satellite enable a device to transmit in a Protection Zone. Condition 1(c)(iii): investigate credible claims and cease operations in the affected area until resolved.

911: condition 1(b)(ii) and paragraph 15 - SpaceX must comply with 47 CFR 9.10(t) (interim SCS 911 routing, annual reports, privacy certification, consumer disclosures) as if it were a CMRS provider using an SCS arrangement, even with no lease. text: The FCC adopted new NEPA rules on 30 September 2026 declaring that space-based operations are not major federal actions, and six days later it authorized SpaceX's 15,000-satellite D2D constellation over DarkSky International's environmental objection. Did the Bureaus apply the new NEPA rules to that authorization? Explain which rule framework they used, how they treated DarkSky's letter, when the new rules take effect, what the new rule text (section 1.1302) says about launches, and who the order says is responsible for launch and re-entry effects. News reports describe a 2-1 vote; check what the order's caption says about the dissent.
reference:
Grade two documents: FCC-26-64 (Modernizing the Commission's NEPA Rules, WT Docket 25-217, Report and Order and FNPRM, adopted 30 September 2026, released 1 October 2026) and DA-26-1078 (6 October 2026) paragraph 45 and footnotes 136-146.

Did the Bureaus apply the new rules? No. DA-26-1078 paragraph 45: the new rules "do not come into effect until 30 days after publication in the Federal Register or after conclusion of the Paperwork Reduction Act process", so the Bureaus "review these comments under our current rules", find the action categorically excluded under 47 CFR 1.1306(a), and decline to require further NEPA review. Footnote 140: DarkSky's letter is treated as a petition for environmental review under 47 CFR 1.1307(c). The paragraph notes that under the new framework the authorization would not require NEPA review and the comments would be moot, but that is dicta; the operative basis is the current categorical exclusion. Footnotes 142-143: the FAA conducts environmental review of launches; an agency need not duplicate another agency's review (47 CFR 1.1311(e)). Footnote 145 calls the aluminum-oxide claim speculative.

FCC-26-64: paragraphs 62-65 find Commission-licensed space-based operations are "extraterritorial activities" excluded from the MFA definition (42 U.S.C. 4336e(10)(B)(vi)) and that spectrum authorizations do not create federal control over deployments. New section 1.1302(c)(5): "Actions associated with space-based operations, including the launch, deployment, and operation of space stations" are not Commission MFAs; 1.1302(b)(6) codifies the extraterritorial exclusion. Footnote 201: the FAA is charged by statute (51 U.S.C. 50903) with licensing launches and controlled re-entries, and the FCC does not view NEPA as giving it authority superseding the FAA's. Paragraph 221: the Report and Order, including revised 1.1301 and 1.1302, is effective 30 days after Federal Register publication; other Appendix A revisions wait for OMB PRA approval and a WTB notice. Caption: "Commissioner Gomez dissenting in part and issuing a statement" - a partial dissent, not a full one; SatNews reported "voted 2-1".

Wrong answers: that the D2D grant relied on the new 1.1302 exclusion; that the new rules were effective on 1 or 6 October 2026; that the FCC now reviews launch emissions; that DarkSky's filing was ignored rather than treated as a 1.1307(c) petition; that the vote was unanimous.

Sources: https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-64A1.pdf ; https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-1078A1.pdf

text: The FCC's April 2026 NGSO-GSO sharing order replaced EPFD limits with performance criteria and added a minimum GSO-arc avoidance angle. For a SpaceX analyst: what is the rule's minimum avoidance angle and the equivalent exclusion zone, in which bands does it apply, may an NGSO operator start service while its compliance demonstration is still pending, and what are the three numerical protection criteria? Then compare that with the GSO-arc exclusion the 6 October 2026 D2D grant actually imposes on SpaceX until the new rules are effective. Finally, when do the rules take effect and which two sections are carved out? Do not conflate the rule's angle with the angle in SpaceX's waiver condition.
reference:
Grade FCC-26-26 (Modernizing Spectrum Sharing for Satellite Broadband, SB Docket 25-157, adopted 30 April 2026, released 1 May 2026) paragraphs 50, 54, 59-65, footnote 225 and ordering clause 90, plus DA-26-1078 (6 October 2026) grant condition 11.

Rule: paragraph 63 - NGSO systems in the 10.7-12.7, 17.3-18.6 and 19.7-20.2 GHz bands must observe a 3-degree GSO-arc avoidance angle with respect to any operational co-frequency GSO satellite serving the United States. Footnote 225: 3 degrees measured on either side of the GSO satellite equals a total 6-degree GSO-arc avoidance zone. Paragraph 64: applicants may submit technical demonstrations and begin operating on an unprotected, non-interference basis while the demonstrations are pending, provided they operate within the demonstrated parameters and the 3-degree angle. Paragraph 65: the Commission may revisit the requirement.

Criteria: paragraph 50 - long-term 3% time-weighted average degraded throughput for GSO links using ACM; paragraph 54 - short-term 0.1% absolute increase in link unavailability (more protective than the 0.4% used in NGSO-NGSO sharing); paragraphs 59-61 - for non-ACM links, -10.5 dB I/N not to be exceeded for 80% of the time, applied in Ku and Ka bands. 328 GSO reference links (paragraph 67); Space Bureau to open a reference-link proceeding within 15 days of release (paragraph 69).

SpaceX D2D grant: DA-26-1078 condition 11(a) requires a minimum GSO arc exclusion zone of at least FOUR degrees with respect to operational GSO satellites, until the new rules are effective and SpaceX demonstrates compliance; 11(b) operations outside the U.S. must meet the EPFD limits unless another country authorizes otherwise; 11(c) unprotected, non-interference, must return to EPFD limits on a Bureau determination of harmful interference, waiver revocable; 11(d) must share ITU validation input data until a favorable or qualified favorable ITU finding. So the waiver condition (4 degrees) is stricter than the rule's 3-degree minimum; an answer that says SpaceX operates under a 3-degree angle today, or that the rule sets 4 degrees, is wrong.

Effective date: ordering clause 90 - effective 60 days after Federal Register publication, except sections 25.146(a)(3) and 25.289(a)(2), which await OMB Paperwork Reduction Act review and a Space Bureau Federal Register notice. The Federal Register summary appeared 13 May 2026 (2026-09565); DA-26-1078 footnote 131 confirms the rules were not yet effective on 6 October 2026 as to those sections.

Sources: https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-26A1.pdf ; https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-1078A1.pdf

text: The FCC adopted its Satellite Spectrum Abundance order on 30 September 2026 (released 1 October 2026, FCC-26-65). Press says it 'unlocks 1,050 MHz' including '550 MHz for downlinks to consumer dishes' in 12.7-13.25 GHz. From the order itself: how many megahertz does the Commission say it unlocks in the 12.7 GHz band, what may NGSO systems do in the band and on what interference footing relative to uplink earth stations, which uplinks remain allowed and from whom, what happens to the application freeze in 12.7-12.75 GHz versus 12.75-13.25 GHz, and when do grandfathered fixed and mobile licensees drop to secondary status. Also give the 42 GHz allocation direction and earth-station licensing type, and the effective-date rule with its exceptions. Note whether Starlink can use the band immediately.
reference:
Grade FCC-26-65 (SB Docket 25-180 et al., adopted 30 September 2026, released 1 October 2026), paragraphs 15-19, 22-26, 29-30, 36-38, footnotes 62, 66, 72, and ordering clauses 132 and 134.

Megahertz: paragraphs 15-16 - "525 megahertz" of additional, contiguous downlink spectrum in the 12.7 GHz band, "a more than 25% increase". The 550 and 1,050 MHz figures in press coverage (TeslaNorth, 30 Sept 2026) are not the order's figures; the order says 525 MHz for 12.7 GHz and 500 MHz for 42 GHz.

NGSO: new primary FSS (space-to-Earth) allocation for NGSO systems in 12.7-13.25 GHz (new footnote NG144), with blanket licensing of user terminals and ESIMs on land, sea and air (paragraphs 15, 18). NGSO FSS downlinks must accept any interference from FSS uplinks from gateway or feeder-link earth stations and operate unprotected vis-a-vis grandfathered terrestrial stations (paragraphs 15, 18). PFD limits from 10.7-11.7 GHz are extended (paragraph 19).

Uplinks: limited to individually licensed gateway and feeder-link earth stations communicating with GSO and NGSO space stations (paragraph 23), plus blanket-licensed ESIMs on aircraft at altitude and ships away from the coast communicating with GSO satellites only (paragraphs 25-26). No ESIM uplinks to NGSO. The "international systems only" limit on GSO uplinks (NG52) is removed (paragraph 22).

Freezes: footnote 62 - the temporary freeze on 12.75-13.25 GHz applications is lifted effective upon Federal Register publication (procedural, no APA delay); paragraph 24 and footnote 72 - 12.7-12.75 GHz gets a permanent freeze on new FSS (Earth-to-space) space and earth station applications via NG144, as a buffer for 12.2-12.7 GHz DBS and FSS downlinks.

Incumbents: paragraphs 29-30 and ordering clause 134 - existing FS and MS licensees are grandfathered co-primary for 10 years from Federal Register publication, after which they become secondary (unprotected, non-harmful-interference basis); the Order of Proposed Modification under section 316 gives licensees 30 days from publication to protest; overall FS/MS allocations change to secondary.

42 GHz: paragraph 36-37 - primary FSS space-to-Earth (downlink only) for GSO and NGSO, to individually licensed and Nationwide Non-Site licensed gateway/feeder-link earth stations (new NG150), no blanket licensing, PFD limits extended from 40.5-42 GHz; MS allocation changed to secondary (paragraph 38); light licensing (paragraph 39).

Effective: ordering clause 132 - 60 days after Federal Register publication, except sections 100.212(c), (i), (j), 100.275(n) and (o), which await OMB review and a Space Bureau notice. Note the rules are written into part 100 even though part 100 is not yet effective (Background section, which states the Commission amends part 100 sections rather than part 25 because part 25 will be removed once part 100 is effective). Starlink cannot use the band immediately: it needs a modification of its space station authorization (SpaceX already requested 12.7-13.25 GHz in DA-26-36, conditions 2-3, and the Gen3 application SAT-LOA-20260630-00264 is pending, per footnotes 140 and 143).

Wrong answers: 550 or 1,050 MHz as the order's figure; NGSO uplinks from user terminals; ESIM uplinks to NGSO; terrestrial incumbents made secondary immediately; 42 GHz allowed for uplinks or blanket-licensed terminals.

Source: https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-26-65A1.pdf

text: The FAA signed a Record of Decision for Starship-Super Heavy at Launch Complex 39A in late January 2026. From the ROD, not the news: what is the signature date, which alternative did the FAA select and which did it identify as environmentally preferable, which three impact categories are listed as unavoidable and significant, how many closure hours per year the ROD gives for tests versus launches and reentries and what share is at night, the NPS annual fee-loss range, the Section 4(f) finding, and how the mitigation measures bind SpaceX. reference:
Grade the FAA Record of Decision for SpaceX Starship-Super Heavy Launch Vehicle at LC-39A, Kennedy Space Center (ROD, 52 pages), signed 1/29/2026 by Katie L. Cranor, Executive Director, Office of Operational Safety, ASA-1, Commercial Space Transportation (Decision and Order, page 52). News said "released January 30, 2026"; the signature date is 29 January 2026.

Alternatives: the FAA selected the Preferred Alternative (issue a new vehicle operator license or modify an existing license for up to 44 launches and 88 landings per year, 44 per stage, plus about 800,000 sq ft of infrastructure). The Environmentally Preferable Alternative is the No Action Alternative, rejected because it is inconsistent with purpose and need and the Commercial Space Launch Act direction (page 10). The ROD does not issue a license: "The completion of the environmental review process does not guarantee that the FAA would issue a license"; the action must also meet safety, risk and indemnification requirements (page 5).

Unavoidable significant effects (page 16): noise and noise-compatible land use, air quality, and airspace transportation. Noise detail (pages 18-20): outdoor levels above 97 dBA max at representative locations; awakening likelihood as high as 82 percent during late-night operations, which make up about half of annual events; sonic booms above 60 dB C-weighted DNL over 28,595 acres off KSC/CCSFS; "Significant effects associated with the Preferred Alternative are unavoidable."

Closures (Health and Safety, pages 16-17): up to 396 hours per year for tests and 462 hours per year for launches and reentries, just under 10 percent of the year (4.5 percent tests, 5.3 percent launches/reentries); half of closure time by day and half at night. The "60.5 days" / "33 to 44 full-day and up to 33 half-day Playalinda closures" figures come from the August 2025 Draft EIS coverage (Florida Today / Yahoo), not from the ROD summary.

NPS: annual fee loss potentially between $239,000 and $423,000, about 13 to 24 percent of revenue (page 20).

Section 4(f) (U.S. DOT Act, Section 4(f) subsection of the consequences summary): no use of Section 4(f) resources; 392 Section 4(f) resources in the noise study area; MINWR and CANA found not subject to 4(f) evaluation for this action; no officials with jurisdiction objected.

Mitigation (Mitigation and Monitoring Summary, pages 20-21): measures include USFWS ESA Section 7 terms, NMFS MMPA stipulations and the NHPA Section 106 Programmatic Agreement; "The issuance of a license to SpaceX will be conditioned upon SpaceX's demonstration that it has complied with required mitigation measures"; mitigation actions "will be made the subject of the terms and conditions of any license issued"; the FAA may enter an agreement for annual environmental inspections.
